why_a_refuses: every one: taint_enforcement — a driving value of the call (often the legitimate request literal itself) also appears in an untrusted output read earlier in the plan prefix; the per-value ledger keeps that match even when the request fixes the value (engine.derive_value returns the ledger match when the trusted origin covers the value)
why_b_admits: an L1 grant covers the call's grant-arg tuple; a grant replaces the content-taint integrity check for its args. L1 binds by handle kind, and the kinds string/id accept a literal of any syntax (a quoted e-mail or title, a date, a year), so a request literal can fill a slot of another type
